conviction_note: Most of H1 is pre-released (5-month trading statement of 27 Aug with an 'ahead of expectations' FY27 call), so the release's new lines are September plate-change trading and whether the FY guide moves again; the September market (private +13.9%, strongest September since 2017) against a comp depressed by the £2.0m JLR cyber hit leans positive, the stock has given back the whole August upgrade (91.9p to 81.7p) so the bar is low, but the September strength was already inside the company's 'ahead' call and discount-led volume tests dealer margins, so p_up is only 57 on a 5.0% absolute scale; findings sum +1.6 against a scaled +0.7, the gap being that the findings are sized on the guidance-raise scenario while p_up carries the chance it is merely reiterated.

findings.finding: September 2026 UK new-car market was the strongest September since 2017 (350,518 regs, +12.1%; private buyers +13.9% to 149,158), and Vertu's September 2025 comparison was depressed by a £2.0m JLR cyber-attack hit across its 10 JLR dealerships, so the interim's September/H2 trading statement should show strong yoy profit growth and supports reiteration or a further raise of the FY27 'ahead' guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-ahead statements: +1.78% (24 Jun 2026 AGM update), +6.86% (27 Aug 2026 trading statement, built on September order-take). Oct 2025 interims, where September carried the JLR hit and guide was 'in line ex one-off': -2.0%.
findings.original_quote: September trading result was impacted by £2.0m due to the JLR disruption. (Vertu interims, 8 Oct 2025); market data: private registrations rose 13.9% to 149,158 in September 2026 (SMMT via EY / electrive, Oct 2026)
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has round-tripped the whole 27 Aug upgrade (91.9p close on 27 Aug to 81.7p on 13 Oct, below the pre-upgrade 84-86p range) while the September market data published 5 Oct came in strong; if the market were pricing a strong September plus a soft comp, the shares would not sit at the buyback's 83p ceiling with the company the main buyer. Coverage is three brokers and turnover ~$231k/day. Caveat applied to the size: the August guide was already explicitly based on September order-take, and FY26 underlying included £3.4m of JLR insurance proceeds, so part of the comp benefit is offset and part of the September strength is inside the 'ahead' guide.
findings.independence: Market series from SMMT (https://www.ey.com/en_uk/newsroom/2026/10/uk-new-car-registrations-continue-growth-in-september ; https://www.electrive.com/2026/10/02/uk-posts-strongest-ever-month-for-bev-registrations-in-september/) is independent of the company's own 2025 comp disclosure.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Vertu's used-car line has not been the driver of its reactions; used volumes were +4.4% LFL in the 5-month statement, already public.

findings.why_not_priced: Released 9 Oct; Vertu traded flat-to-down afterwards (84.2 -> 81.7p), so no read-across rally is visible. Proxy only: Motorpoint is a pure used retailer and attributes its outperformance to its own technology, and it also flagged consumer uncertainty ahead of the Budget - so small.
